title: Trace the outline of an image

seo.metaTitle: Trace the Contour of a PNG Shape - Free, No Upload
seo.metaDescription: Reduce a cutout to a line drawing: keep only the boundary band, 1 to 5 px wide, painted in the color you pick. Free and unlimited, entirely inside your browser.
seo.longDescription: Finding the contour reduces a cutout to a line drawing: the shape is shrunk by the Thickness you set, and the pixels that vanish in that step - the band along the boundary - are kept and painted in the Stroke color. Everything else, including the whole interior of the object, becomes fully transparent, so what comes out is an outline rather than a picture with a border. The line is Thickness pixels wide, from 1 to 5 px, and it sits inside the silhouette. PNG, JPG, WebP and BMP are accepted, and the tracing happens in your browser.
howTo: Drop the cutout into the source area, or pick a file from your device.
Set Thickness from 1 to 5 px; 1 px gives the finest line.
Pick the Stroke color in the swatch; black is the starting value.
Download the result - only the line survives, everything else is transparent.

faq.q: Where does the line sit, inside or outside the shape?
faq.a: Inside. The contour is the band the shape loses when it is shrunk by Thickness, so the outline eats into the object instead of being painted around it.

faq.q: Why did the picture content disappear?
faq.a: That is the point of the tool: only the boundary is kept. If you want the picture with a ring drawn around it, use the outline tool instead, which leaves the original pixels alone.

faq.q: What happens to a shape thinner than the line?
faq.a: It turns into a solid blob, because every one of its pixels belongs to the boundary band. Hairlines and thin letters need Thickness 1 to stay readable.

faq.q: Can I get the outline and the picture in one file?
faq.a: Not from this tool. Save the traced line, then compose the two images with the blend tool if you want them layered in a single picture.
